basics.name: Richard Lee Davis, Ph.D.
basics.label: Education Researcher & Data Scientist
basics.summary: Education researcher and data scientist with 5+ years of experience leading international projects in learning analytics, educational technology, and assessment. Ph.D. in Learning Sciences (Stanford) with a strong background in quantitative analysis, psychometrics, and machine learning. Proven ability to manage multi-disciplinary teams and deliver innovative solutions for large-scale assessments (co-developer of an OECD pilot assessment). Excellent communicator with a track record of high-quality publications, grant reports, and presentations. Passionate about leveraging data and research to improve education policy and outcomes globally.

work.name: KTH Royal Institute of Technology
work.summary: Conducting research in digital learning and educational technology, focusing on learning analytics and AI-driven instructional tools
highlights: Conducting research in digital learning and educational technology, focusing on learning analytics and AI-driven instructional tools.
Supervising graduate student projects and managing research initiatives within the Division of Digital Learning; fostering collaborations with international academic and industry partners.

work.name: OECD (Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development)
work.summary: Co-developed experimental computer science assessment for OECD's PILA initiative
highlights: Co-developed an experimental computer science assessment ('Karel' programming tasks) for the OECD's Platform for Innovative Learning Assessments, aimed at evaluating 15-year-old students' problem-solving and coding skills.

Managed the pilot implementation of the assessment in four countries (Singapore, Ireland, the Netherlands, Brazil) with 500+ students; coordinated with national project teams, oversaw data collection procedures, and ensured adherence to technical standards.

Analyzed pilot data and authored a detailed report of findings and recommendations for the OECD Secretariat and participating countries, contributing to the design of future large-scale digital assessments.

work.name: École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL)
work.position: Postdoctoral Researcher, Computer-Human Interaction in Learning & Instruction (CHILI) Lab
work.summary: Led multi-year research projects in learning sciences and developed data-driven educational tools
highlights: Project Leadership: Led and coordinated multi-year research projects in learning sciences, including managing a team of 2 PhD students and a software engineer to develop novel learning analytics applications for education.

Tool Development: Designed and implemented data-driven tools for education, such as interactive learning dashboards and AI-supported training simulators, to enhance teaching and learning in vocational and higher education.

Communication & Publishing: Authored numerous research papers in top-tier conferences/journals (earning a Best Paper Award at EDM 2020 and nominations at LAK 2023 and CSCL 2025). Co-edited an academic volume on educational technologies for vocational training.

Workshops & Collaboration: Organized and facilitated international workshops and a winter school as co-director of a joint EPFL-ETH doctoral program, strengthening collaboration among researchers from multiple countries.

work.name: Bildungsraum Nordwestschweiz (Northwestern Switzerland Education Dept.)
work.summary: Evaluated usability and effectiveness of regional digital assessment platforms
highlights: Evaluated the usability, user experience, and pedagogical effectiveness of regional digital assessment platforms (Mindsteps and Check-dein-Wissen) used in secondary education.

Conducted stakeholder interviews and data analysis, and delivered a 10,000-word evaluation report with actionable recommendations to educational authorities, informing improvements to the platforms and implementation strategies.
